# Made by `python3 -I tools/reference.py shell-table` from docs/reference/*.txt. Do not edit.
== string
syn: string subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: string length STRING | The count of characters.
sub: string length -grapheme STRING | The count of grapheme clusters.
sub: string bytelength STRING | The count of bytes of the UTF-8 form.
sub: string insert STRING INDEX TEXT | STRING with TEXT before the character at INDEX.
sub: string index STRING INDEX | The character at INDEX, or an empty string past the end.
sub: string index -grapheme STRING INDEX | The grapheme cluster at INDEX, with INDEX in clusters.
sub: string range STRING FIRST LAST | The characters from FIRST to LAST.
sub: string range -grapheme STRING FIRST LAST | The grapheme clusters from FIRST to LAST.
sub: string first NEEDLE HAYSTACK ?START? | The index of the first NEEDLE from START, or -1.
sub: string last NEEDLE HAYSTACK ?LAST? | The index of the last NEEDLE at or before LAST, or -1.
sub: string compare ?-nocase? ?-length N? A B | -1, 0, or 1 in the order of the characters.
sub: string equal ?-nocase? ?-length N? A B | 1 when the strings are the same, else 0.
sub: string match ?-nocase? PATTERN STRING | 1 when the glob PATTERN matches all of STRING.
sub: string map ?-nocase? MAPPING STRING | Replaces each key of the key and value list MAPPING with its value.
sub: string repeat STRING COUNT | STRING COUNT times.
sub: string replace STRING FIRST LAST ?NEW? | STRING with the characters from FIRST to LAST replaced by NEW.
sub: string reverse STRING | The characters in the reverse order.
sub: string reverse -grapheme STRING | The grapheme clusters in the reverse order, each with its characters in order.
sub: string tolower STRING ?FIRST? ?LAST? | Lowercase.
sub: string toupper STRING ?FIRST? ?LAST? | Uppercase.
sub: string totitle STRING ?FIRST? ?LAST? | The first character uppercase and the rest lowercase.
sub: string trim STRING ?CHARS? | STRING with the CHARS (white space by default) removed at both ends.
sub: string trimleft STRING ?CHARS? | The same at the start only.
sub: string trimright STRING ?CHARS? | The same at the end only.
sub: string is CLASS ?-strict? ?-failindex VAR? STRING | 1 when each character is of CLASS: alnum, alpha, ascii, boolean, digit, double, integer, wideinteger, list, lower, upper, space, xdigit, and others.
sub: string cat ?STRING ...? | The strings joined with no separator.
sub: string wordstart STRING INDEX | The index of the first character of the word at INDEX.
sub: string wordend STRING INDEX | The index after the last character of the word at INDEX.
== tcl::prefix
syn: tcl::prefix subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: tcl::prefix match ?-exact? ?-message TEXT? ?-error OPTIONS? TABLE STRING | The entry of TABLE that STRING is a unique prefix of, or an error.
sub: tcl::prefix all TABLE STRING | Each entry that starts with STRING.
sub: tcl::prefix longest TABLE STRING | The longest common prefix of those entries.
== append
syn: append varName ?value ...?
== concat
syn: concat ?arg ...?
== format
syn: format formatString ?arg ...?
== scan
syn: scan string format ?varName ...?
== split
syn: split string ?splitChars?
syn: split string splitChars -grapheme
== join
syn: join list ?joinString?
== regexp
syn: regexp ?-option ...? exp string ?matchVar? ?subMatchVar ...?
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -all | Finds each match.
opt: -inline | Gives the match and its groups as a list, and sets no variable.
opt: -indices | Gives the start and end index of each match in place of the text.
opt: -start INDEX | Starts the search at INDEX.
opt: -line | ^ and $ match at each line, and .
opt: -expanded | White space and # comments in exp are ignored.
opt: -about | Gives the count of groups and the flags of exp.
== regsub
syn: regsub ?-option ...? exp string subSpec ?varName?
opt: -all | Replaces each match.
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -start INDEX | Starts the search at INDEX.
== subst
syn: subst ?-nobackslashes? ?-nocommands? ?-novariables? string
== encoding
syn: encoding option ?arg ...?
sub: encoding convertto ?-profile PROFILE? ?-failindex VAR? ENCODING STRING | The bytes of STRING in ENCODING, as a byte string.
sub: encoding convertfrom ?-profile PROFILE? ?-failindex VAR? ENCODING BYTES | The text of BYTES in ENCODING.
sub: encoding profiles | The profiles: replace strict tcl8.
sub: encoding user | The encoding of the user: utf-8.
sub: encoding names | The names of the encodings: the ones with no table, and the files of the encoding folders.
sub: encoding system | The encoding of the system: utf-8.
sub: encoding dirs ?LIST? | The folders of the encoding files of Tcl (koi8-r.enc, iso2022-jp.enc, ...).
== binary
syn: binary subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: binary format TEMPLATE ?VALUE ...? | Gives the bytes.
sub: binary scan BYTES TEMPLATE ?VAR ...? | Sets the variables and gives the count of values that it read.
sub: binary encode FORMAT ?-option value ...? DATA | base64, hex, or uuencode text of the bytes.
sub: binary decode FORMAT ?-option value ...? DATA | The bytes of the text.

syn: lfilter varList list ?varList list ...? command
== lrepeat
syn: lrepeat count ?value ...?
== lreverse
syn: lreverse list
== lsearch
syn: lsearch ?-option value ...? list pattern
opt: -exact | The element equals the pattern.
opt: -glob | A glob pattern (the default).
opt: -regexp | A regular expression.
opt: -all | Gives each index that matches.
opt: -inline | Gives the elements in place of the indexes.
opt: -not | Finds the elements that do not match.
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -index INDEX | Compares element INDEX of each element.
opt: -sorted | The list is sorted, and the search is a binary search.
opt: -start INDEX | Starts at INDEX.
opt: -stride N | Tcl 9.1 only: the list is groups of N elements.
== lsort
syn: lsort ?-option value ...? list
opt: -ascii | Compares the text (the default).
opt: -dictionary | Compares the text with no case, and runs of digits as numbers: a2 before a10.
opt: -integer | Compares integers.
opt: -real | Compares floats.
opt: -command CMD | Calls CMD with two elements.
opt: -increasing | The smallest first (the default).
opt: -decreasing | The largest first.
opt: -index INDEX | Compares element INDEX of each element.
opt: -unique | Keeps one of each run of equal elements.
opt: -nocase | Compares letters with no case.
== lmap
syn: lmap varList list ?varList list ...? command
== foreach
syn: foreach varList list ?varList list ...? command
== dict
syn: dict subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: dict create ?KEY VALUE ...? | A new dict.
sub: dict get DICT ?KEY ...? | The value at the path of keys.
sub: dict getdef DICT ?KEY ...? KEY DEFAULT | The value at the path of keys, or DEFAULT when a key is missing.
sub: dict exists DICT KEY ?KEY ...? | 1 when the path of keys exists.
sub: dict set VAR KEY ?KEY ...? VALUE | Sets the value at the path in the dict of a variable, and gives the new dict.
sub: dict unset VAR KEY ?KEY ...? | Removes a key in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict keys DICT ?PATTERN? | The keys, or the keys that match a glob pattern.
sub: dict values DICT ?PATTERN? | The values.
sub: dict size DICT | The count of keys.
sub: dict for {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} DICT BODY | Runs BODY for each key and value.
sub: dict map {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} DICT BODY | A new dict with the same keys and the results of BODY as values.
sub: dict filter DICT key|value|script ... | The keys and values that match a pattern, or a script that gives true.
sub: dict merge ?DICT ...? | One dict.
sub: dict remove DICT ?KEY ...? | A copy with no such keys.
sub: dict replace DICT ?KEY VALUE ...? | A copy with the new values.
sub: dict incr VAR KEY ?INCREMENT? | Adds to an integer value in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict append VAR KEY ?STRING ...? | Adds text to a value in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict lappend VAR KEY ?VALUE ...? | Adds elements to a list value in the dict of a variable.
sub: dict update VAR KEY VARNAME ?KEY VARNAME ...? BODY | Links variables to keys while BODY runs, and writes them back after it.
sub: dict with VAR ?KEY ...? BODY | Makes a variable of each key while BODY runs, and writes them back after it.
sub: dict info DICT | Text for people with the count of entries of the dict.
== array
syn: array subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: array set NAME LIST | Sets the elements from a list of names and values.
sub: array get NAME ?PATTERN? | A list of names and values.
sub: array names NAME ?MODE? ?PATTERN? | The element names.
sub: array exists NAME | 1 when the variable is an array.
sub: array for {KEYVAR VALUEVAR} NAME BODY | Runs BODY once for each element of a copy of the array.
sub: array default get|set|exists|unset NAME ?VALUE? | The value that a read of a missing element gives.
sub: array size NAME | The count of elements.
sub: array unset NAME ?PATTERN? | Removes the elements, or the whole array.
sub: array statistics NAME | Text about the hash table.
sub: array startsearch NAME | A search id, for the old way to go through an array one element at a time.
sub: array nextelement NAME ID | The next element name of the search.
sub: array anymore NAME ID | 1 when the search has more elements.
sub: array donesearch NAME ID | Ends the search.

syn: expr arg ?arg ...?

== trace
syn: trace option ?arg ...?
sub: trace add variable NAME OPS CMD | OPS is a list of read, write, unset, and array.
sub: trace add command NAME OPS CMD | OPS is a list of rename and delete.
sub: trace add execution NAME OPS CMD | OPS is a list of enter, leave, enterstep, and leavestep.
sub: trace remove TYPE NAME OPS CMD | Removes a trace.
sub: trace info TYPE NAME | The traces of a name.
sub: trace variable NAME OPS CMD | The old form of trace add variable.
sub: trace vdelete NAME OPS CMD | The old form of trace remove variable.
sub: trace vinfo NAME | The old form of trace info variable.
== if
syn: if expr1 ?then? body1 elseif expr2 ?then? body2 ... ?else? ?bodyN?
== while
syn: while test command
== for
syn: for start test next command
== break
syn: break
== continue
syn: continue
== switch
syn: switch ?-option ...? string ?pattern body ...? ?default body?
opt: -exact | The pattern equals the string (the default).
opt: -glob | A glob pattern.
opt: -regexp | A regular expression.
opt: -integer | Tcl 9.1 only: the pattern and the string are the same integer, such as 16 and 0x10.
opt: -nocase | Matches letters with no case.
opt: -- | The end of the options, for a string that starts with -.

syn: case string ?in? ?pattern body ...? ?default body?

syn: eval arg ?arg ...?

syn: apply lambdaExpr ?arg ...?

syn: time command ?count?

syn: rename oldName newName
== namespace
syn: namespace subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: namespace eval NS SCRIPT | Runs SCRIPT in NS, and makes NS when it does not exist.
sub: namespace current | The name of the current namespace.
sub: namespace children ?NS? ?PATTERN? | The namespaces in NS.
sub: namespace parent ?NS? | The namespace around NS.
sub: namespace exists NS | 1 when NS exists.
sub: namespace delete ?NS ...? | Removes namespaces with their commands and variables.
sub: namespace export ?-clear? ?PATTERN ...? | The commands that other code can import, and that an ensemble has.
sub: namespace import ?-force? ?PATTERN ...? | Makes the exported commands of another namespace callable by their short names.
sub: namespace forget ?PATTERN ...? | Removes imported commands.
sub: namespace ensemble create ?-option value ...? | Makes the namespace a command with its exported commands as subcommands.
sub: namespace path ?LIST? | The namespaces where a command name is looked up after the current one.
sub: namespace which ?-command? ?-variable? NAME | The full name of a command or variable, or an empty string.
sub: namespace origin CMD | The full name of the command that an imported command points to.
sub: namespace qualifiers NAME | The part of NAME before its last ::.
sub: namespace tail NAME | The part of NAME after its last ::.
sub: namespace code SCRIPT | A script that runs in the current namespace from each place, for a callback.
sub: namespace inscope NS SCRIPT ?ARG ...? | Runs SCRIPT in NS.
sub: namespace upvar NS OTHERVAR MYVAR ?OTHERVAR MYVAR ...? | Links local names to variables of NS.
sub: namespace unknown ?SCRIPT? | The handler of an unknown command in the namespace.

== eof
syn: eof channelId
== seek
syn: seek channelId offset ?origin?
== tell
syn: tell channelId
== fconfigure
syn: fconfigure channelId ?-option value ...?
opt: -mode baud,parity,data,stop | A serial port: the baud, the parity (n, o, e, m, or s), the data bits (5 to 8), and the stop bits (1 or 2), for example 115200,n,8,1.
opt: -handshake type | A serial port: none, rtscts, xonxoff, or dtrdsr (Windows only).
opt: -xchar {xon xoff} | A serial port: the two characters of xonxoff.
opt: -ttycontrol {signal value ...} | A serial port: sets the lines RTS, DTR, and BREAK, for example {DTR 0 RTS 1}.
opt: -ttystatus | A serial port, read only: a dict of the lines CTS, DSR, RING, and DCD.
opt: -queue | A serial port, read only: the counts of bytes in the input queue and the output queue of the system.
== fblocked
syn: fblocked channelId
== fcopy
syn: fcopy input output ?-size size? ?-command callback?
== chan
syn: chan subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: chan close CHAN ?DIRECTION? | As close.
sub: chan configure CHAN ?-option value ...? | As fconfigure.
sub: chan copy IN OUT ?-size N? ?-command CB? | As fcopy.
sub: chan eof CHAN | As eof.
sub: chan flush CHAN | As flush.
sub: chan gets CHAN ?VAR? | As gets.
sub: chan names ?PATTERN? | The names of the open channels.
sub: chan pipe | Makes a pipe and gives two channels: the bytes that go into the second come out of the first.
sub: chan puts ?-nonewline? ?CHAN? STRING | As puts.
sub: chan read ?-nonewline? CHAN ?N? | As read.
sub: chan seek CHAN OFFSET ?ORIGIN? | As seek.
sub: chan tell CHAN | As tell.
== source
syn: source ?-encoding name? fileName
== file
syn: file subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: file join NAME ?NAME ...? | One path from parts.
sub: file split NAME | The parts of a path.
sub: file dirname NAME | The path without its last part.
sub: file tail NAME | The last part.
sub: file extension NAME | The extension with its dot, such as .json.
sub: file rootname NAME | The path without its extension.
sub: file normalize NAME | The full path with .
sub: file pathtype NAME | absolute, relative, or volumerelative.
sub: file nativename NAME | The path with the separator of the platform.
sub: file separator ?NAME? | The separator of paths.
sub: file exists NAME | 1 when the file exists.
sub: file isfile NAME | 1 for a file.
sub: file isdirectory NAME | 1 for a folder.
sub: file readable NAME | 1 when the file can be read.
sub: file writable NAME | 1 when the file can be written.
sub: file executable NAME | 1 when the file can run.
sub: file owned NAME | 1 when the user owns the file.
sub: file size NAME | The size in bytes.
sub: file mtime NAME ?TIME? | The time of the last change, in seconds.
sub: file atime NAME ?TIME? | The time of the last read, in seconds.
sub: file stat NAME VAR | Puts the facts of the file in an array.
sub: file lstat NAME VAR | As stat, for a link itself.
sub: file type NAME | file, directory, link, and others.
sub: file attributes NAME ?OPTION ?VALUE ...?? | The attributes of the platform, such as -permissions.
sub: file mkdir ?DIR ...? | Makes folders, with each missing parent.
sub: file copy ?-force? ?--? SOURCE ?SOURCE ...? TARGET | Copies files and folders.
sub: file rename ?-force? ?--? SOURCE ?SOURCE ...? TARGET | Moves files and folders.
sub: file delete ?-force? ?--? ?NAME ...? | Removes files, and folders with -force.
sub: file link ?-symbolic|-hard? LINK ?TARGET? | Makes a link, or gives its target.
sub: file readlink NAME | The target of a symbolic link.
sub: file tempfile ?VAR? ?TEMPLATE? | Opens a new temporary file and gives its channel.
sub: file channels ?PATTERN? | The names of the open channels.
sub: file system NAME | The file system of a path.
sub: file volumes | The volumes, such as /.
== glob
syn: glob ?switches? name ?name ...?
opt: -nocomplain | No match gives an empty list.
opt: -directory DIR | Matches in DIR.
opt: -types TYPES | Only files of the types, such as f and d.
opt: -tails | Gives the names without the folder of -directory.
== cd
syn: cd ?dirName?
== pwd
syn: pwd
== zipfs
syn: zipfs subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: zipfs mount ?ZIPFILE? ?MOUNTPOINT? | Mounts a zip file, or gives the mounts.
sub: zipfs unmount MOUNTPOINT | Removes a mount.
sub: zipfs list ?(-glob|-regexp)? ?PATTERN? | The names of the files in the mounts.
sub: zipfs exists NAME | 1 when the file is in a mount.
sub: zipfs info NAME | The zip file, the size, the packed size, and the offset of a file.
sub: zipfs root | The root of the mounts: //zipfs:/.

== tcl::Bgerror bgerror

== interp
syn: interp cmd ?arg ...?
sub: interp create ?-safe? ?-meter NAME? ?--? ?PATH? | A new child, and its path.
sub: interp eval PATH ARG ?ARG ...? | Runs a script in the child.
sub: interp alias SRCPATH SRCCMD TARGETPATH TARGETCMD ?ARG ...? | Makes SRCCMD of the child run TARGETCMD of the parent.
sub: interp aliases ?PATH? | The aliases of a child.
sub: interp delete ?PATH ...? | Removes children.
sub: interp exists PATH | 1 when the child exists.
sub: interp children ?PATH? | The children.
sub: interp cancel ?-unwind? ?--? ?PATH? ?RESULT? | Stops the script of the interp with the error "eval canceled", or RESULT.
sub: interp slaves ?PATH? | The old name of children.
sub: interp issafe ?PATH? | 1 for a safe interpreter.
sub: interp hide PATH CMD ?NAME? | Hides a command from the scripts of the child.
sub: interp expose PATH NAME ?CMD? | Makes a hidden command visible again.
sub: interp hidden ?PATH? | The hidden commands.
sub: interp invokehidden PATH ?-global? NAME ?ARG ...? | Runs a hidden command.
sub: interp marktrusted PATH | Makes a safe child trusted.
sub: interp recursionlimit PATH ?N? | The nesting limit of the child.
sub: interp target PATH ALIAS | The target of an alias.
== package
syn: package option ?arg ...?
sub: package require ?-exact? NAME ?VERSION ...? | Loads a package and gives its version.
sub: package provide NAME ?VERSION? | Says that the package is loaded, or gives its version.
sub: package ifneeded NAME VERSION ?SCRIPT? | The script that loads a version.
sub: package present ?-exact? NAME ?VERSION? | The version of a loaded package, or an error.
sub: package names | The names of the known packages.
sub: package versions NAME | The versions of a package that ifneeded knows.
sub: package forget ?NAME ...? | Forgets packages.
sub: package vcompare V1 V2 | -1, 0, or 1.
sub: package vsatisfies VERSION REQ ?REQ ...? | 1 when VERSION fits a requirement such as 1.2, 1.2-, or 1.2-2.0.
sub: package prefer ?latest|stable? | Which versions require picks.
sub: package unknown ?CMD? | The command that runs for a missing package.

== oo::class oo::object
syn: oo::class create name ?definition?
syn: oo::class new ?definition?
== oo::define oo::define::constructor oo::define::deletemethod oo::define::destructor oo::define::export oo::define::filter oo::define::forward oo::define::method oo::define::mixin oo::define::renamemethod oo::define::self oo::define::superclass oo::define::unexport oo::define::variable
syn: oo::define className arg ?arg ...?
sub: constructor ARGS BODY | The code that runs when an object is made.
sub: destructor BODY | The code that runs when an object is removed.
sub: method NAME ARGS BODY | A method.
sub: variable ?NAME ...? | Variables that each method sees with no my variable.
sub: superclass ?CLASS ...? | The parent classes.
sub: mixin ?CLASS ...? | Classes whose methods come before the methods of the class.
sub: filter ?METHOD ...? | Methods that run around each call.
sub: forward NAME CMD ?ARG ...? | A method that runs a command.
sub: export NAME ?NAME ...? | Makes methods callable from outside.
sub: unexport NAME ?NAME ...? | Makes methods callable only with my.
sub: deletemethod NAME ?NAME ...? | Removes methods.
sub: renamemethod OLD NEW | Gives a method a new name.
sub: self SCRIPT | Changes the definition of the class object itself.
== oo::objdefine oo::objdefine::class oo::objdefine::deletemethod oo::objdefine::export oo::objdefine::filter oo::objdefine::forward oo::objdefine::method oo::objdefine::mixin oo::objdefine::renamemethod oo::objdefine::unexport oo::objdefine::variable
syn: oo::objdefine object arg ?arg ...?
== oo::copy

== thread thread::attach thread::broadcast thread::cancel thread::cond thread::configure thread::create thread::detach thread::errorproc thread::eval thread::exists thread::exit thread::id thread::join thread::mutex thread::names thread::preserve thread::release thread::rwmutex thread::send thread::transfer thread::unwind thread::wait
syn: thread::create ?-joinable? ?-preserved? ?-isolation LEVEL? ?-caps LIST? ?-compute UNITS? ?-meter NAME? ?script?
sub: thread::create ?-joinable? ?-preserved? ?-isolation LEVEL? ?-caps LIST? ?-compute UNITS? ?-meter NAME? ?SCRIPT? | A new thread that runs SCRIPT, and its id.
sub: thread::send ?-async? ?-head? ID SCRIPT ?VAR? | Runs SCRIPT in the thread and gives its result.
sub: thread::broadcast SCRIPT | Sends SCRIPT to each other thread.
sub: thread::wait | Runs the event loop of the thread until thread::release.
sub: thread::id | The id of this thread.
sub: thread::names | The ids of the threads.
sub: thread::exists ID | 1 when the thread exists.
sub: thread::join ID | Waits for a joinable thread to end.
sub: thread::preserve ?ID? | Adds a reference.
sub: thread::release ?-wait? ?ID? | Takes a reference away.
sub: thread::cancel ?-unwind? ID ?RESULT? | Stops the script that runs in a thread.
sub: thread::unwind | Ends thread::wait of this thread.
sub: thread::exit ?STATUS? | Ends this thread.
sub: thread::configure ID ?OPTION? ?VALUE? | The options of a thread, such as -eventmark.
sub: thread::errorproc ?PROC? | The proc for errors of scripts of -async sends.
sub: thread::transfer ID CHANNEL | Moves a channel to a thread.
sub: thread::mutex create|destroy|lock|unlock ?ID? | Mutexes.
sub: thread::eval ?-lock MUTEX? SCRIPT | Runs SCRIPT with a mutex locked.
== tsv tsv::append tsv::array tsv::exists tsv::get tsv::handlers tsv::incr tsv::keyldel tsv::keylget tsv::keylkeys tsv::keylset tsv::lappend tsv::lindex tsv::linsert tsv::llength tsv::lock tsv::lpop tsv::lpush tsv::lrange tsv::lreplace tsv::lsearch tsv::lset tsv::move tsv::names tsv::object tsv::pop tsv::set tsv::unset
syn: tsv::set array element ?value?
sub: tsv::set ARRAY ELEMENT ?VALUE? | Sets or gives a value.
sub: tsv::get ARRAY ELEMENT ?VAR? | The value.
sub: tsv::exists ARRAY ?ELEMENT? | 1 when it exists.
sub: tsv::unset ARRAY ?ELEMENT ...? | Removes elements or the array.
sub: tsv::incr ARRAY ELEMENT ?N? | Adds to an integer.
sub: tsv::append ARRAY ELEMENT VALUE ... | Adds text.
sub: tsv::lappend ARRAY ELEMENT VALUE ... | Adds list elements.
sub: tsv::pop ARRAY ELEMENT | The value, and removes it.
sub: tsv::move ARRAY OLD NEW | Gives an element a new name.
sub: tsv::names ?PATTERN? | The names of the arrays.
sub: tsv::array set|get|names|size|reset ARRAY ... | Commands on a whole array.
sub: tsv::lock ARRAY ARG ?ARG ...? | Runs a script with the lock of the array.
sub: tsv::keylset ARRAY ELEMENT KEY VALUE | Keyed lists: keylget, keylkeys, and keyldel go with it.
sub: tsv::object ARRAY ELEMENT | A command for one element.
sub: tsv::handlers | The names of the storage handlers.
== tpool tpool::cancel tpool::create tpool::get tpool::names tpool::post tpool::preserve tpool::release tpool::resume tpool::suspend tpool::wait
syn: tpool::create ?-minworkers N? ?-maxworkers N? ?-idletime S? ?-initcmd SCRIPT? ?-exitcmd SCRIPT?
sub: tpool::create ?OPTIONS? | A new pool, and its id.
sub: tpool::post ?-detached? ?-nowait? POOL SCRIPT | Gives a job to the pool, and its job id.
sub: tpool::wait POOL JOBLIST ?VAR? | Waits for one job of the list to end, and gives the ids of the jobs that ended.
sub: tpool::get POOL JOB | The result of a job that ended.
sub: tpool::cancel POOL JOBLIST ?VAR? | Removes jobs that have not started.
sub: tpool::suspend POOL | Stops the start of new jobs.
sub: tpool::preserve POOL | Adds a reference.
sub: tpool::names | The ids of the pools.
== info
syn: info subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: info commands ?PATTERN? | The names of the commands.
sub: info procs ?PATTERN? | The names of the procs.
sub: info exists VAR | 1 when the variable has a value.
sub: info vars ?PATTERN? | The visible variables.
sub: info globals ?PATTERN? | The variables of the top level.
sub: info locals ?PATTERN? | The local variables of the proc.
sub: info args PROC | The argument names of a proc.
sub: info body PROC | The body of a proc.
sub: info default PROC ARG VAR | 1 when the argument has a default, which goes in VAR.
sub: info level ?N? | The depth of the call stack, or the command at level N.
sub: info complete SCRIPT | 1 when the script has no open brace, bracket, or quote.
sub: info script ?NAME? | The file of the script that source runs.
sub: info functions ?PATTERN? | The names of the math functions.
sub: info cmdcount | The count of commands that ran.
sub: info patchlevel | The version of Tcl that ztcl follows: 8.6.16.
sub: info tclversion | 8.6.
sub: info library | The folder of the Tcl library: empty in ztcl.
sub: info loaded | The loaded binary packages.
sub: info nameofexecutable | The path of the program.
sub: info sharedlibextension | The extension of a shared library.
sub: info hostname | The name of the host.
sub: info errorstack ?INTERP? | The -errorstack of the last error: INNER and the failed command, then CALL and the words of each proc that the error left, and UP and a count of levels for a catch in the frame of uplevel.
sub: info coroutine | The full name of the running coroutine, or an empty string.
sub: info class SUBCOMMAND CLASS ?arg ...? | Facts about a TclOO class, as info class of Tcl 8.6.
sub: info object SUBCOMMAND OBJECT ?arg ...? | Facts about a TclOO object, as info object of Tcl 8.6.
== clock
syn: clock subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: clock seconds | The seconds since the epoch.
sub: clock milliseconds | The milliseconds since the epoch.
sub: clock microseconds | The microseconds since the epoch.
sub: clock clicks ?-milliseconds|-microseconds? | A counter for time spans.
sub: clock format SECONDS ?-format FMT? ?-gmt BOOL? ?-timezone ZONE? ?-locale L? | The time as text.
sub: clock scan TEXT ?-format FMT? ?-gmt BOOL? ?-timezone ZONE? ?-base SECONDS? | The seconds of a time in text.
sub: clock add SECONDS ?COUNT UNIT ...? ?-gmt BOOL? ?-timezone ZONE? | The seconds after adding days, months, and other units.

== ztcl::wasm
syn: ztcl::wasm subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: load fileName | Reads, decodes, and validates a module file, and gives a module handle.
sub: new bytes | Decodes and validates the bytes of a module, and gives a module handle.
sub: instantiate module ?option value ...? | Links the imports (-imports, -link, -wasi), runs the start function, and gives an instance handle.
sub: call instance function ?-limit units? ?-raw? ?--? ?arg ...? | Calls an export and gives its result, a list of its results, or an empty string.
sub: package fileName ?prefix? ?-wasi dict? | Loads a Tcl C package built for wasm32-wasi with libztclstubs.a and runs its init function.
sub: run module|fileName ?option value ...? | Runs a WASI command (_start) and gives its exit code.
sub: memory instance size|grow|read|write|string ?arg ...? | Reads, writes, and grows the linear memory of an instance.
sub: global instance name ?value? | Reads or sets an exported global.
sub: exports module|instance | A list of name, kind, and type for each export.
sub: imports module | A list of module, name, kind, and type for each import.
sub: info module | A dict of the counts and the features of a module.
sub: delete handle ?handle ...? | Deletes modules and instances.
sub: jit ?boolean? | Reads or sets the use of the JIT tier for the calls of the interpreter.
== ztcl::text ztcl::text::graphemes ztcl::text::words ztcl::text::sentences ztcl::text::width ztcl::text::bounds
syn: ztcl::text subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: graphemes STRING | The list of the grapheme clusters: the characters that a user sees, such as an emoji with a skin tone or a letter with accents.
sub: words ?-all? STRING | The list of the word segments that have a letter or a number.
sub: sentences STRING | The list of the sentences, each with its spaces and line end.
sub: width ?-ambiguous narrow|wide? STRING | The count of columns of the string in a terminal or a monospace font.
sub: bounds ?-unit grapheme|word|sentence? STRING | The list of the character index of each boundary, from 0 to the length of the string.

== ztcl::tls ztcl::tls::socket
syn: ztcl::tls socket ?-servername name? ?-alpn protocols? ?-cadata pem? ?-verify boolean? host port
sub: socket ?option value ...? host port | Opens the connection and gives the name of the channel.
opt: -servername name | The DNS name for SNI and for the check of the certificate.
opt: -alpn protocols | A list of up to 8 ALPN protocols.
opt: -cadata pem | The trust anchors as PEM text, in place of the store of the system.
opt: -verify boolean | With 0, the chain and the host name are not checked.

== ztcl::gc
syn: ztcl::gc subcommand
sub: ztcl::gc stats | A dict of the counts: collections, gc_ns, mark_ns, sweep_ns, pause_p50_ns, pause_p99_ns, pause_max_ns, heap_bytes, heap_peak, live_bytes, used_bytes, threshold, allocated, freed, alloc_rate, uptime_ns, rss, rss_peak, returned, and retained.
sub: ztcl::gc collect | Runs a collection now, where the build can collect.
sub: ztcl::gc reset | Starts the counts again.
== ztcl::meter
syn: ztcl::meter subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: ztcl::meter create NAME ?-budget UNITS? ?-tenant TEXT? | Makes the meter NAME, or sets the options of the meter NAME.
sub: ztcl::meter get NAME | The dict of the counts of NAME.
sub: ztcl::meter list | The names of the meters.
sub: ztcl::meter reset NAME | Sets each count of NAME to zero.
sub: ztcl::meter delete NAME | Removes NAME.
sub: ztcl::meter run NAME SCRIPT | Runs SCRIPT in the current interpreter and counts it in NAME.
sub: ztcl::meter record NAME ?-tenant TEXT? ?-script TEXT? ?-sign? ?-key SEED? | The usage record of NAME: one line of JSON with the SHA-256 of the record before it.
sub: ztcl::meter verify RECORD PUBLICKEY | 1 when the signature of RECORD matches the hex public key, else 0.
sub: ztcl::meter pubkey SEED | The hex public key of a hex seed.
== ztcl::agent
syn: ztcl::agent subcommand ?arg ...?
sub: ztcl::agent run ?-option value ...? | Runs the loop.
sub: ztcl::agent doc NAME TEXT ?ARG TYPE ...? | Sets the text of the tool NAME and the types of its arguments.
sub: ztcl::agent describe NAME | The spec of the command NAME as a tool: name, text, JSON schema, and parameters.
sub: ztcl::agent check SCHEMA VALUE | VALUE when it matches the result schema SCHEMA, else the error ZTCL AGENT RESULT.
sub: ztcl::agent schema SCHEMA | The JSON schema of a result schema.
sub: ztcl::agent post URL HEADERS BODY | One HTTP/1.1 POST of a JSON body.
